title: aidd-team roles
description: The delivery team's roles, the loop they follow, the handoffs between them, and the domain packs they load. The edit-time guard reads `writes` and `in_scope`; `aidd gen-docs` renders the rest into the agent files, the docs, and one skill per domain pack.

step.description: A loop step (docs/METHOD.md §5). Spec approval and Merge approval are the human approvals between steps, not steps.

loop_point.description: A loop step, or one of the two human approvals between steps.

standard.description: One standard, practice, or regulation, kept once in the top-level `standards` table. `edition` names the version or year of a document and then `source` is required. `checked` is when someone last confirmed the entry against its source, and then `source`, `checked_by`, and `evidence` (what they read, where) are required, so a date is never a bare assertion. A practice with no versioned document or canonical page has no source to check against: it carries `reviewed` instead of `checked`, and its context in `notes`. Every entry has exactly one of the two dates; `aidd eval standards` fails on a checked entry without its source and evidence, and on either date older than a year.

edition.description: The version, year, or release applied, and nothing else: `5.0.0`, `ISO/IEC 25010:2023`, `Regulation (EU) 2016/679`.

published.description: When that edition was published (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when the source gives only a month).

notes.description: Context for a person: application dates, the next draft, a caveat. Not machine-checked.

source.description: Where the current edition is published.

checked.description: The date the edition was last confirmed current and its source found neither archived nor deprecated (YYYY-MM-DD).

reviewed.description: For a practice with no source to check: when someone last re-read the practice as the registry states it and found it still how the discipline works (YYYY-MM-DD). Held to the same year as `checked`.

checked_by.description: Who confirmed the edition on `checked`: a person's handle, or `agent:<harness>/<model>` for an agent's check.

quote.description: The line on that page that shows the edition or date.

evidence.description: What the checker saw. Required with `checked_by`, so a date is never a bare assertion.

maturity.description: established (the default when absent): years of wide adoption under an authoritative maintainer. emerging: a draft, a first edition, a pre-1.0 release, a community-maintained extension, or a practice adopted by few; applied only when the change clearly needs it, and said in the Spec.

standard_ref.description: A standard a role or pack applies: the id of an entry in `standards`, or the id with `as`, the narrower way this role applies it.

contract_item.description: One loop-contract rule: its text, or the text with `applies_to`, the roles or loop steps it binds. A rule without `applies_to` binds every role; with it, only a role named there or working in a step named there, and only those roles' agent files carry it.

license_allowed.description: Licenses compatible with shipping inside an Apache-2.0 project and with commercial use.

order.description: Role keys in the order docs list them. Every key in `roles` appears once.

version.description: The loop contract's version (semver). A change that removes, adds, or reorders a step, an approval, or a lane is a major change and bumps the major number; a rewording that changes no duty bumps the patch. Gate events record it as `loop_version`.

entry.description: The loop's entry rule: how a change picks its lane before the first step (docs/METHOD.md §5 and §6).

contract.description: Rules the roles keep, each rendered into the agent file of every role it applies to (every role, unless the rule names `applies_to`).

artifacts.description: What crosses between roles, by id: each handoff names the artifacts it hands on, and each role the artifacts it reads. `kind` says where it lives: a section of the Spec, a path, a PR/MR comment the author posts, or a human or platform source no role writes.

name.description: A short name, as an agent file lists it.

where.description: The Spec section, the path, or the comment it lives in.

handoffs.description: Who hands what to whom: a file (`through`) plus the handoff note the contract requires (`note` names what the note adds). `to` may name a human party, such as the author at a gate.

to.description: Role keys, or a human party.

through.description: The file or output the next party reads.

artifact.description: The ids in `loop.artifacts` this handoff hands on: a Spec section, a path, or a PR/MR comment, never text returned in chat alone.

note.description: What the handoff note adds beyond the file.

flows.description: One entry per team command: which roles it runs, in which order (each inner list runs in parallel), and where it stops for a human. The commands are tested against it.

runs.description: Groups in order; the roles of one group run in parallel.

loops.description: The two loops the method runs. The inner loop is autonomous agentic execution: an agent iterates inside a frozen contract until it is green or blocked. The outer loop is human strategy and governance: it decides what is worth doing, whether work may start, whether it may merge, and whether the process changes. Every step belongs to exactly one of them, and the gates are the only points where control passes between the two.

outer.description: What the outer loop is and who runs it.

inner.description: What the inner loop is and what bounds it.

boundary.description: What crosses between the loops, and what never does.

outer_steps.description: The loop steps a human owns the decision for.

inner_steps.description: The loop steps an agent executes autonomously.

gates.description: The human approvals between the two loops, in order.

when.description: The edge's label in the loop diagram: what sends the work back.

note.description: What happens on that path, in a sentence.

feedback.description: The paths on which a human decision or a production signal sends work back to an earlier point. The loop diagram draws them as dashed edges.

capabilities.description: Every process of a software life cycle standard, and what covers it: the agents alone, the agents with a person deciding, or people.

standards.description: Every standard the team applies, once, keyed by id. Roles and domain packs reference the ids, so one edition and one checked date serve them all.

starts_when.description: When the role may start; before it holds, the role stops and hands back.

industry.description: The job titles the role maps to.

standards.description: Industry standards the role applies, by id in `standards`.

reads.description: The artifacts the role acts on, by id in `loop.artifacts`. Each is handed to it by another role or comes from a person or the platform, and every handoff's artifacts are read by each role it goes to.

writes.description: The role's write area: placeholders or globs. The edit-time guard checks it, as a guide: it denies an edit or an obvious shell write outside the area, and the gate's scope rule decides. Empty means read-only.

in_scope.description: True for roles whose edits ship in the change: they also stay inside the scope of their Tasks.

extends.description: Skills, plugins, MCP servers, or tools that extend the role, as starting points a team verifies, pins, and installs through a change. Each is optional and used only when the project already uses it. The list is open: any capability can be added the same way, with its `tier`.

tier.description: Who stands behind it. official: made by the harness vendor itself, so its source is in the vendor's own repository (Anthropic's github.com/anthropics/ or code.claude.com for Claude Code). Being listed in the vendor's official directory (`listed_in`) is not the same: a third-party entry listed there keeps its maker's tier, vendor or community, and records the listing and the directory's pinned commit. vendor: the service's own connector (GitHub's GitHub MCP). maintainer: an established tool from its own project (Semgrep, Trivy, OWASP ZAP, Vale). community: anything else, which must be `emerging`, carry an allowed `license`, and be pinned.

license.description: The SPDX license identifier of the pinned release, or `Proprietary` for a hosted service or closed code (`Proprietary (source-available)` when the source is readable but not licensed for reuse). Required for a tool, a plugin, or a skill; `aidd eval standards` fails without it.

license_note.description: A term a team must know before installing: a separate license for bundled content, a restriction on redistribution, or a source-available license that is not open source.

pin.description: The release, tag, or commit a team installs, so an update is a change a person reviews; a tag resolves to its commit. A hosted MCP server that only its vendor runs is pinned as `vendor-hosted <URL>`, the endpoint a team connects to. Required for a tool, a plugin, or a skill; `aidd eval standards` fails without it.

listed_in.description: The harness vendor's official directory that lists it and pins the commit named in `pin`. A listing says the vendor reviewed and pinned it, not that the vendor made it.

adds.description: What the role can do with it.

capabilities.description: What the extension itself can touch, as its own source and docs show, so a team sees it before installing: `network` makes network calls beyond the model API (fetches, remote MCP servers, hosted services, a browser loading pages); `writes_repo` can create, modify, or delete files in the repository, in the working tree or by committing or opening pull requests through an API; `runs_commands` executes shell commands or starts other programs (hooks, scripts, package managers, test runners, a browser, commands in a cluster); `reads_secrets` needs a credential (an API key, a token, an OAuth grant, cloud credentials) or can read secret material; `telemetry` sends usage data to its vendor beyond the requests the work needs, and `telemetry_opt_out` then says whether it can be turned off. Empty means read-only: a skill that only guides the agent, or a tool that only reads. What the agent does with its own tools while following a skill is not the skill's capability. When the source does not settle one, it is listed: the superset is the safe reading.

telemetry_opt_out.description: Required with `telemetry`, and only with it: whether a team can turn the telemetry off (a flag, a setting, or an environment variable the extension's docs name).

checked.description: When someone last confirmed the source is current; `aidd eval standards` fails on one older than a year.

practices.description: Practice skills the role loads for its kind of work (`plugins/aidd-team/skills/<name>`), hand-written playbooks with a checked date; a Task names up to two of them in `skills`.

preload.description: Practice skills or domain packs the role uses on most runs, preloaded into its agent at startup through the agent file's `skills:` list (after the aidd skill, which every role preloads). Each is one of the role's `practices` or a domain pack's `slug`. At most two, since a preloaded skill's whole text enters every run's context; a Task loads the rest by name with the `Skill` tool.

tier.description: What the work needs, harness-neutral: `reasoning` decides or judges where a mistake is invisible to tests and no human check follows, and takes the strongest model the harness offers; `execution`, the default, builds or proposes where the tests, the gate, or a human catch the mistake, and inherits the session's model. A role is promoted to `reasoning` only with a `tier_reason` that says why, and on eval evidence. The Claude Code plugin maps the tier to its own `model:` frontmatter (an alias or `inherit`); every other harness reads the tier and picks.

tier_reason.description: Why this role sits in this tier, in one sentence: what its mistakes cost and what catches them.

writes_unfrozen.description: Extra areas the role writes on the fast and emergency lanes, where no tester runs and nothing is frozen: the developer writes the regression test with the fix. On the spec lane Spec approval freezes them and they stay another role's.

triggers.description: Concrete nouns a change names when it touches the domain (FHIR, PHI, card data, Terraform). The pack's description leads with them, since a harness picks a skill by its description and truncates a long one.

step.description: A loop step, or `Entry`: the entry rule, when `aidd next` computes the route and picks the lane before the first step.

checklist.description: What every role checks in this domain, at the entry rule and by loop step.

tests.description: Test commands for the Spec's `[[tests.commands]]`: a best practice the gate runs, not prose.
